Steps to Reproduce:

QA Env:

Environment

Steps to Reproduce

  1. On Work Orders, select two customers in the Customer filter — one real, one throwaway (e.g. ZZAUTOTEST).
  2. Navigate away; delete the ZZAUTOTEST customer while off the page.
  3. Return to the Work Orders page.

Actual Result
The deleted customer is no longer shown in the Customer dropdown options, but the table results are still filtered by that deleted customer — the value is removed from the UI but continues to be applied to the result set.

Expected Result (S10-N1 / C29616)

  • The deleted value is silently ignored — no error. (OK)
  • The filter reflects only the still-valid selection. (OK)

Impact
Users see a result set silently constrained by a value they can no longer see or control — misleading, and inconsistent with the documented "silently ignored" behavior.

Description

The start and end time pickers in the shift modal let you pick any minute value. The PRD requires 15-minute increments, and the design shows a dropdown stepping 6:45, 7:00, 7:15, 7:30. Secondary issue: in QA the picker only opens from the clock icon, while in the design clicking the time field itself opens it.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the Schedule module, week of Aug 2 to 8, 2026
  2. Click any shift block to open the modal
  3. Click the clock icon in the start time field
  4. Look at the minute column

Expected Result

The picker offers 15-minute increments only, such as 7:00, 7:15, 7:30, 7:45, and it opens when the time field is clicked.

Actual Result

The minute column lists every minute, 00, 01, 02, 03, 04, 05 and so on, so any minute can be selected. The picker also opens only from the clock icon, not by clicking the field.

PRD:

screen-capture (29).webm

comments.body: Whole time slot should open the time modal , but as we are offer the time for the user and funcional its ok , moving this as Low , do this if time allows Stefan Vukovic Branko Cicovic

Fixed, on sv8685.qa — both halves.

The shift card's clocks are now the same 15-minute dropdown as the Create Event modal, and the whole field opens it, not just the clock icon. The field itself is one shared component now, so this modal, staff Technician Hours and the event modal cannot drift apart again.

One behaviour change to know while testing: an all-day shift converts to timed only when a time is actually picked. Opening a clock to look and clicking away leaves it all-day — previously any blur would convert it. A block already stored at the hours you want therefore needs a different time picked and the original picked back.

Test steps

  1. Schedule → click a shift block → click the start time field anywhere → the dropdown opens.
  2. Options step 00/15/30/45 only; typing 7 / 715 / 7:15 reaches the 7-o'clock quarters.
  3. Pick a time → the block moves and an undo toast appears; undo restores it.
  4. Open a clock on an ALL-DAY block and click away without picking → still all-day.
  5. Pick a time on an all-day block → converts to timed.
  6. As a Schedule-View-only user, the fields stay read-only.

→ QA Status: Passed

  • Verified the Fixes on the QA Branch

Description

The shift tooltip and shift detail modal show TIME LOGGED as 1h / 1h with a full progress bar, but the work order shows Actual 0.00 of 1.00 and Progress 0%. No time has been clocked against the line, so the schedule is reporting work that never happened.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open WO S8685-12876 and note line 1 shows Actual/Estimate 0.00 / 1.00 and Progress 0%
  2. Open the Schedule module, week of Aug 2 to 8, 2026
  3. Hover the Pamill Paving shift on the Jose Young row, Sunday Aug 2
  4. Also click the block to open the modal
  5. Compare the TIME LOGGED values

Expected Result

Time logged reflects actual clocked time, so it shows 0h / 1h with an empty progress bar.

Actual Result

Both the tooltip and the modal show 1h / 1h with a full progress bar, indicating the line is complete while the work order reports 0% and zero actual hours.

screen-capture (30).webm

comments.body:
Fixed, on sv8685.qa.

What was wrong: the schedule read work_order_line.tech_time and labelled it "logged". That is an estimate-side figure, which is why the bar was always exactly full. It now sums the same clocked timesheet records the work order's Actual comes from, so both surfaces read the same source.

Two behaviours worth knowing while testing:

  • An open clock-in counts as running until now, on both surfaces — matching the WO page deliberately, so a technician still clocked in shows progress rather than zero.
  • The bar's percentage is capped at 100%, so an over-run shows the hours honestly but the bar stops full.

Test steps

  1. Open WO S8685-12876 → line 1 shows Actual 0.00 / 1.00, Progress 0%.
  2. Schedule → week of Aug 2–8 → hover the Pamill Paving shift on the Jose Young row (Sunday Aug 2).
  3. Expected: TIME LOGGED reads 0h / 1h with an empty bar — not 1h / 1h.
  4. Click the block → the detail card agrees.
  5. Clock some time against that line, reload → both the WO's Actual and the schedule's TIME LOGGED move by the same amount.
  6. Clock in and leave it running → both show the running time.

→ QA Status: Passed

  • Verified the Fixes on the QA Branch

Description

Day view always opens with the timeline at 12 AM. It should scroll so the working-day start sits at the left edge with a small buffer before it. Shop business hours are off and Jose Young's hours start at 7:00 AM, so the timeline should open near 6:30 AM.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the Schedule module
  2. Click Day
  3. Note the leftmost time column
  4. Click the forward arrow to move to the next day
  5. Note the leftmost time column again

Expected Result

On load and on day navigation the timeline auto-scrolls so the working-day start is at the left edge, showing roughly 6:30 AM first.

Actual Result

The timeline starts at 12 AM on load and stays at 12 AM after navigating to the next day. The user has to scroll manually to reach working hours.

PRD:

screen-capture (32).webm

comments.body:
Part fixed and deployed to sv8685.qa — but closing this as reported needs a product decision. Detail below.

The auto-scroll rule itself works. The resolver returns the earliest opening minute less a 30-minute buffer (06:30 for a 07:00 open), and FullCalendar re-applies it on day navigation. Verified in the browser: zoom the page in until the 24 hours no longer fit, and the timeline scrolls to the working-day start both on load and when stepping to the next day.

Why you see 12 AM at a normal window: the hour columns are sized to fill the container, so at normal zoom the whole day already fits. The scrollable range is zero — the left edge is midnight by construction, and there is nowhere to scroll to. No scroll logic can change that.

What was fixed here: on a cold load the resolved opening minute arrives with the board read, which lands after FullCalendar has captured its scroll target — so day view was using the 07:00 no-data fallback instead of the resolved 06:30. That value is now applied when the hours arrive. Visible only when the axis actually overflows (zoomed in, or a narrow window), so on its own it does not change what you see at normal zoom.

What is needed to close this as reported: for the board to OPEN near 6:30 AM, day view has to show fewer hours at once so the remainder scrolls — a minimum width per hour column. At a 1440px window, showing roughly 06:30–19:00 first works out to about 64px per hour, i.e. a ~1540px axis against a ~800px time area.

That changes how day view reads for every user and every screen size, so it is a density decision rather than a defect fix, and I would rather not pick the number unilaterally. Branko Cicovic — how many hours should day view show at once before scrolling? Once that is set, the existing scroll logic delivers the working-day start at the left edge with no further work.

Note also that the behavior is width-dependent by nature: on a very wide monitor the whole day fits regardless, so "opens at 6:30" can only ever hold for windows narrower than the full axis.

Verified on sv8685.qa, Day view, Thu Aug 6.

  • 150 percent: opens at 6 AM, correct
  • 110 percent: 12 AM
  • 100 percent: 12 AM
  • 75 percent: 12 AM

Scroll logic is correct. It only fires when the axis overflows, which does not happen at normal zoom.

Not resolved as reported. No user at a normal window sees the working-day start on load.

Branko Cicovic needs to set the density: how many hours should Day view show before scrolling? Stefan estimates ~64px per hour, roughly 06:30 to 19:00 at 1440px.

Fixed on QA.

Day view was squeezing all 24 hours into whatever width the window had, so on a smaller or zoomed screen the columns got so narrow the hour labels were cut off ("10 A", "12 P"). The columns now have a minimum width: on a wide screen they still stretch to fit the whole day exactly as before, and on a narrower one they stop shrinking and the grid scrolls sideways instead. The switch happens around 1770px of window width.

Because the day can now be wider than the window, the view also opens at the start of business hours rather than at midnight.

Test steps:

  1. Open the Schedule in Day view on a wide screen (1920) — all 24 hours must still fit with no horizontal scrollbar, same as before.
  2. Zoom in (or use a narrower window) — the columns must stop shrinking, every hour label must stay fully readable, and the grid must scroll sideways.
  3. On the narrow/zoomed screen, confirm the view opens just before the start of business hours, not at midnight.
  4. Switch to another day with the arrows, and switch away to Week and back to Day — it must land at business hours each time.
  5. On the wide screen, confirm it does NOT jump or scroll (there is nothing to scroll).
  6. Check Week and Month views are unchanged at both sizes.
  7. Confirm blocks, the current-time line, the today highlight and the capacity bars all still line up with the hours.

Description

When only a page search is active and nothing matches it, the empty screen says no work orders match your filters and offers a Clear Filters link. No filter is on, so that link does nothing useful and there is no way to clear the search from the empty screen.

This ticket is closed as OBSOLETE and is kept as a record.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: QA branch sv8785 (https://sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders). Desktop browser, signed in as an Admin.

  1. Open Work Orders on a desktop browser, All tab, and use Clear Filters first so that no filter is on.
  2. Click the Search button in the page toolbar and type text that matches nothing, for example: ZZQQNOMATCHXX
  3. Read the message in the empty table area and look at the link underneath it.

Current behaviour

The message reads "No work orders match your filters" even though no filter is on, and the only link offered is Clear Filters. Clicking it changes nothing, because there are no filters to clear: the search text stays and the screen stays empty. Nothing on the empty screen clears the search.

A later live check found this still happening. One part of the original report does now behave correctly: clearing filters no longer clears the search text.

A screen recording taken at the time is attached. The ticket is closed and has not been reopened — that is the QA lead’s decision, not ours.

Expected behaviour

The empty screen tells the user that nothing matched their search and offers a way to clear the search. Where both a search and filters are on, it offers each of them separately, so clearing one does not clear the other.

Source — the Filters specification on Confluence, version 19, requirement S8-R3: “When the combination of active filters and any active search query produces no matching records, the table shows an empty state with a message indicating no results were found for the current filters and search”

The same description, requirement S8-R4: “The empty state includes a prompt or link to clear filters and, where a search query is active, to clear the query”

The same description, requirement S8-R5: “Where both a query and filters are active, each is cleared independently from the empty state. Clearing filters does not clear the query and clearing the query does not clear the filters, consistent with S13-R13”

Description

Every time on the Schedule is shown six hours later than the time the job was scheduled for. A job put on a technician's calendar for 7:00 in the morning appears as 1:00 in the afternoon — on the block, in the hover summary, in the shift window and in the Day view. The 'now' marker is wrong by the same six hours.

This makes the Schedule unusable as a planning board: a morning job looks like an afternoon job, and a 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM day shift reads 1:00 PM to 1:00 AM and spills onto the next day.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: QA branch sv8685 — https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule. Desktop browser, signed in as an Admin, with the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 selected.

  1. Open Schedule from the top navigation and choose the Week view.
  2. In the left-hand panel, type S-15855 into 'Search work orders' to find the Vuchester Retail work order, unit 10123073, line 'Service - Mobile service call made by George Donald 403-369-7067'.
  3. Check technician Ayesha Khan's hours first, in Administration then Staff, then Edit Staff Member: Monday 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM and Tuesday to Friday 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM. So a job placed on her should start at 7:00 in the morning.
  4. Drag that work order card onto Ayesha Khan's row, on the Tuesday column.
  5. Hover the new block and read the time range in the pop-up summary.
  6. Click the block and read the two time boxes in the shift window.
  7. Switch to the Day view for that date. Read where the block sits against the hour labels, and read the time printed on the 'now' marker.

Current behaviour

Every time reads six hours later than it should. The 7:00 AM job reads 1:00 PM. A 9:00 AM job reads 3:00 PM. The 'now' marker read 4:11 PM while the clock at the shop read 10:11 AM.

The date can roll over too: a 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM shift reads 1:00 PM to 1:00 AM and is drawn partly on the following day.

For a developer: the times are stored correctly and shown wrongly. A shift saved as 16:01 UTC (10:01 in the shop's own time zone, America/Edmonton, which is six hours behind) is displayed as 4:01 PM. Forcing the browser's own time zone to America/Edmonton gives the same wrong result, so this is not the viewer's machine.

Expected behaviour

The Schedule shows the time at the shop. A job scheduled to start at 7:00 in the morning reads 7:00 AM everywhere — on the block, in the hover summary, in the shift window and in the Day view — and the 'now' marker matches the clock on the shop wall.

Source

Epic SV-8685 Open , story SV-8686 TESTING QA (Schedule Grid Layout & Navigation), and the Schedule specification (Confluence page 713031682), version 25.

Section 4.2: "Every shift has a start time. It is derived from a hierarchy: The technician's configured working hours take precedence." The technician in the steps above has hours of 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, so a shift placed on her must read 7:00 AM, not 1:00 PM.

Section 4.8, on the Day view: "Now line. A vertical indicator showing the current time, with a label on hover over the grid." The current time for a shop is the time on the shop's own clock.

One honest note: the specification writes no rule about time zones anywhere, so it is silent on that point. What those two lines do settle is that a shift's start follows the technician's hours and that the marker shows the current time, and the six-hour shift breaks both.

Affected Area: Schedule → recurring/series shifts (spread), Week and Month view

Description: In Week and Month view, a recurring series shift cannot be reassigned by drag-and-drop. The drag appears to work — the block moves against other technician rows — but on releasing the mouse it snaps back to its original technician and date. This works correctly in Day view. Per SV-8692 QA Complete / PRD §7, dragging a shift to another technician should reassign it.

Steps to Reproduce:

  1. Create a recurring series (drag a multi-line work order onto a technician, choose "Schedule whole work order," create the shifts).
  2. Switch to Week view (then repeat in Month view).
  3. Drag one of the series shifts onto another technician and release the mouse.

Actual Result: The shift returns to its original technician and date — no reassignment happens.

Expected Result: The shift reassigns to the target technician (with the cross-tech confirmation), the same as in Day view.

Impact: Recurring shifts can't be reassigned from Week or Month view; only Day view works.

Story: SV-8692 QA Complete — Linked Series & Banners
Epic: SV-8685 Open — Schedule — Technician Scheduling Module

Branko Cicovic Bilal Muzamil

comments.body: Stefan Vukovic Month view we do not support in v1, and in week view it should be fixed.

Fixed on SV-8685-schedule-module-rewrite, on sv8685.qa now. Scoped to Week view per Branko Cicovic — Month view stays drag-inert for v1, so a series banner there still bounces back by design.

Cause. The series banner was emitted as a display-only block: not draggable at all, so the drag never produced a drop the page could act on. Day view worked because it draws the individual shift, not the banner.

What the banner does now. It is draggable, and because the banner IS the whole job, the gesture acts on the whole job:

  • Onto another technician → the reassign dialog, worded for a recurring job, and confirming moves every occurrence — including days outside the visible week. The dialog states that explicitly, and names no date, because a reassign changes the lane and not the dates.
  • Onto a different day, same technician → the whole job shifts, each occurrence keeping its place in the pattern.

The day-shift rule (worth reading before testing). A series moves by working days, not calendar days: Wed–Fri dragged one day later runs Thu, Fri, Mon for a technician who does not work weekends — the same interruption rule the spread step already uses when it creates a series, so a job created skipping weekends still skips them after a move. Two deliberate exceptions:

  • dropping onto a day the technician does not work is honored as dropped (it is for a single shift too — the conflict detector flags it), and the other occurrences then keep the calendar distance from the day you chose;
  • an occurrence already sitting on a non-working day keeps its own day rather than being pulled onto its neighbour's.

Also fixed while in here: the move was visibly tearing in half — only the grabbed day jumped, the rest caught up about a second later when the server answered. The grid now moves the whole job immediately, by the same rule the server applies, so nothing shifts a second time.

Spec note — an amendment is owed. PRD §7 covers shift reassignment between technicians, and §4.6 defines a series as a render-time grouping; neither describes dragging the banner, so "the whole job moves" and the working-day rule are product decisions taken with me on 2026-08-06 rather than something the PRD says. Branko Cicovic — worth writing into §4.6 / §7 so QA and the next dev read it from the spec. Related: partial reassignment (moving only part of a series to another tech) was considered and dropped, since the spec requires a series to be continuous.

Suggested test steps

  1. Week view → create a series spanning Mon–Fri on a technician with Mon–Fri hours.
  2. Drag its banner onto another technician → the dialog names the job, no date, and says every day moves → confirm. Every occurrence should be on the new technician, including any in adjacent weeks (check by navigating a week either way).
  3. Undo from the toast → the whole job returns to the original technician.
  4. Same lane, drag the banner one day later → Tue–Fri plus Monday of the following week; nothing on Saturday or Sunday. Watch closely: the whole banner should move at once, not one day first.
  5. Drop a banner onto a Saturday → it lands there and is flagged as a conflict (deliberate).
  6. Month view → a banner still does not drag (v1 scope).
The fix has been verified on QA.

Description

A saved Customer, Lead Technician or Service Advisor filter comes back switched on but without its value on the button. The button reads only "Customer" instead of "Customer: Iibay Landscaping", so the list is filtered by something the screen no longer names. The Status and Asset on Site buttons keep their value correctly, so a user sees one button naming its value beside another that does not.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: QA branch sv8785 — https://sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders. Desktop browser, signed in as an Admin.

  1. Sign in as an Admin and open Work Orders on the All tab with no filters on.
  2. Click the Customer button and pick the customer Iibay Landscaping. The button correctly reads "Customer: Iibay Landscaping" and the list narrows.
  3. Leave the page and come back. Any of these four does it: open a work order and click back; refresh the page; close the browser completely and sign in again; or open the same link in a new window.
  4. Read the Customer button.
  5. Repeat the whole thing with the Lead Technician button, picking Admin ShopView, and again with the Service Advisor button, picking Admin ShopView.
  6. For a contrast, repeat it once more with the Status button, picking Paid.

Current behaviour

The button comes back blue, so it is clearly switched on, but it reads only "Customer" — the customer's name is gone.

The filter itself is still working: the list is still narrowed to that customer, and opening the button shows the name with a tick beside it.

The same happens on the Lead Technician and Service Advisor buttons. It does not happen on Status or Asset on Site — "Status: Paid" comes back correctly.

It happens every time, on all four ways back to the page, on all three of those buttons.

For a developer: the three affected filters are the ones whose choices are fetched from the server; the button's label is drawn before the name for the saved value has arrived and is not drawn again once it does.

Expected behaviour

The button still reads "Customer: Iibay Landscaping" after coming back to the page, so the user can see which customer the list is filtered by without opening the button.

Source

Epic SV-8785 Open , stories SV-8792 TESTING QA (Active Filter Chip Appearance) and SV-8795 Ready for QA (Filter Persistence), and the Filters specification (Confluence page 572030978), version 19.

Requirement S7-R1: "When a filter has one or more values selected, the chip changes to an active/highlighted visual state (blue pill) and displays the selected value(s)". The last five words are the part that is missing.

Requirement S10-R1: "When the user navigates away from the Work Orders page (e.g., to a Work Order detail, then back), the filter selections and collapsed/expanded state are restored exactly as they were left".

Description

On a phone there is no page search for the work order list. The magnifier button in the action row opens the application-wide search instead, and that does not narrow the list. Page search works normally on a desktop screen.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: QA branch sv8785 — https://sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders. Phone-sized browser, 390 x 844 with touch on, signed in as an Admin.

  1. On a phone, or in a browser window 390 pixels wide with touch turned on, sign in as an Admin and open Work Orders. There are 30 work orders in the list on the All tab.
  2. Look at the action row. The only search control is the magnifier button.
  3. Tap the magnifier button.
  4. Type the customer name Bahampton Holdings, which has 6 work orders, so a working page search would visibly narrow the list to those 6.
  5. Watch the work order list and the address bar as you type.
  6. For a contrast in the same sitting, type the same name into the page search on a desktop-sized window.

Current behaviour

There is no page search on the phone at all. Tapping the magnifier opens the application-wide search box, with its own close button beside it.

Typing Bahampton Holdings into it does not narrow the list. The list stays at 30 work orders and the address bar stays as it was, with no search added to it.

The same name typed into the page search on a desktop window does narrow the list correctly, so the search term is not the problem — the control is simply missing on the phone.

For a developer: the desktop page-search control is not present in the page at all on a phone-sized screen, and the Create Work Order button keeps a width of 332 pixels on a 390 pixel screen, so there is no free space in the action row for a search field to open into.

Expected behaviour

On a phone the page search opens in place inside the action row, about 162 pixels wide, and narrows the work order list as the user types, exactly as it does on a desktop screen. The Create Work Order button shrinks to its natural width to make room. The application-wide search is a separate control and does not stand in for it.

Source

Epic SV-8785 Open , story SV-8798 Ready for QA (Page Search), and the Filters specification (Confluence page 572030978), version 19.

Requirement S13-R16: "Mobile uses the same inline expansion as desktop. There is no modal, no separate search screen, and no mobile-only state in the component. Tapping the collapsed control expands it in place within the action row, moves focus into the field and raises the keyboard".

Requirement S13-R17: "On mobile the expanded field fills the remaining width of the action row rather than taking the fixed 180px desktop width. On Work Orders that resolves to 162px. All other toolbar actions remain visible and in position throughout; nothing is hidden while searching".

Requirement S13-R18: "To create that room, the primary CTA on mobile uses its natural hug width instead of stretching to fill the row: 'New Work Order' is 144px, the same width it has on desktop, not 211px."

Requirement S13-R9 keeps the two searches apart: "Search is scoped strictly to the records in the current table. It never returns results from another table, another page, another module, or any content outside that table." So the application-wide search cannot stand in for the page search.

Affected Area: Schedule → work order sidebar → WO list

Description: The sidebar work order list loads 25 work orders per batch with a "Load more" button. PRD §11 says the list should virtualize (continuous scroll), so the build and spec don't match.

Clarification Needed: Please confirm which is intended. If the "Load more" / 25-per-page pattern is acceptable, PRD §11 should be updated to describe it. If continuous virtualized scroll is required, the build should be changed to match.

Story: SV-8687 QA Complete — Work Order Sidebar & Mini Calendar
Epic: SV-8685 Open
Reference: PRD §11 — "sidebar work order list virtualizes at 50+ items"

Bilal Muzamil

comments.body:
Answered by making it continuous — deployed to sv8685.qa. No PRD change needed.

Both were already true, at different layers. Rendering has always been virtualized (q-virtual-scroll, so only the visible cards exist in the DOM however long the list is) — PRD §11's virtualization requirement was met. What the video shows is fetching: 25 per page behind a "Load more" press, which §11 doesn't speak to. So the build didn't contradict §11; it just also paged.

What changed: the next page now loads as the list nears its end, and the button is gone.

Three things worth knowing when you re-test:

  • It also loads when the list cannot be scrolled — a pane taller than the loaded cards, or a caller whose cards aren't focusable (the button used to be the only Tab-reachable control in that region, so removing it without this would have stranded later pages for keyboard users).
  • A role="status" "Loading more…" line appears while a page is in flight, so the state is announced rather than silent.
  • Each page is requested exactly once, however hard you scroll.

Test: with more than 25 schedulable work orders, scroll the sidebar list — later pages arrive without pressing anything, and it stops when the shop runs out. Filters and search still re-key the list from page 1.

The fix has been verified on QA:

Description

Dragging a job out of the Unassigned row onto a technician moves it correctly, but silently changes its saved start time to six hours earlier. A job booked for 7:00 in the morning became 1:00 in the morning, which is outside the working hours of the technician it was given to. Nothing on screen warned about it.

This is separate from SV-8848 OBSOLETE . There the times are stored correctly and shown wrongly; here the stored value itself is changed, so the record stays wrong even after the display is fixed.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: QA branch sv8685 — https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule. Desktop browser, signed in as an Admin, with the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 selected.

  1. Open Schedule and go to the week containing Saturday 8 August 2026.
  2. Find a job sitting in the Unassigned row. The one used here was work order S-12876, customer Pamill Paving, unit 713, line 'Replace - Rear ramp handles', sitting unassigned on Saturday 8 August. The Unassigned row sits below every technician row, so you have to scroll down to reach it; if it is not drawn, put a job there first by dragging a work order onto it.
  3. Open the job and note its start time. This one read 7:00 AM.
  4. Check the receiving technician's hours: Kellie Ayers (Foreman) works 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM.
  5. Drag the block up onto Kellie Ayers' row for the same day.
  6. Confirm the 'Move this shift to Kellie Ayers on Sat, Aug 8?' window with Reassign.
  7. Open the job again and read its start time.

Current behaviour

The job does move to the chosen technician and does leave the Unassigned row, and the technician is correctly added to the work order line's technician list. That part is right.

But the saved start time moves six hours earlier — from 7:00 in the morning to 1:00 in the morning. 1:00 AM is outside the receiving technician's own hours of 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM.

It is not just what is drawn on screen: the time quoted above was read back from the saved record after the move. It is not the technician's hours being applied either — her start is 7:00 AM, and 7:00 is the number that ended up saved, but saved as 7:00 UTC instead of 7:00 at the shop. The same block dragged between two technician rows moves normally.

Expected behaviour

Assigning an unassigned job to a technician moves it to that technician and leaves its start time as it was — and in any case leaves it inside that technician's own working hours.

Source

Epic SV-8685 Open , story SV-8688 TESTING QA (Drag-and-Drop Scheduling & Shift Creation), and the Schedule specification (Confluence page 713031682), version 25.

Section 3.2, on the unassigned row: "Dragging a shift from this row down onto a technician assigns it."

Section 4.2: "When an unassigned shift is later dragged onto a technician row in the grid, that technician's hours apply."

One honest note: the specification does not say the start time must be left exactly as it was, so the first half of the expected behaviour above is stricter than the written rule. The second half is not — 1:00 in the morning is neither the time the job had nor within the hours of the technician it was given to.

The Schedule can show a unit's VIN on the shift blocks. In Month view the blocks are small and the specification says the VIN is deliberately left off there. Month view shows it anyway, which crowds the block and pushes the job description out of sight.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: QA branch sv8685 — https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule. Desktop browser, signed in as an Admin, with the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 selected.

  1. Open Schedule.
  2. Open the FILTER & DISPLAY dropdown in the toolbar and turn the VIN Number switch ON. It is off by default, so this step is needed.
  3. Choose Week view with the Day / Week / Month control and read the blocks. The VIN appears, which is correct.
  4. Switch to Month view and read the blocks. The week of 2 to 8 August 2026 on this shop already holds several units with a VIN recorded, so no extra test data is needed.
  5. Switch to Day view and read them again. The VIN appears there too, which is also correct.

Current behaviour

With the VIN Number switch on, Month view prints the VIN on the blocks that have one — 11 of 67 blocks carried a full 17-character VIN.

Read straight off Month view blocks: 'Xiriver Apparel ~ 24069 ~ 3HSDZAPT9KN042164 ~ 19 Lines ~ Part of a series', 'Xiriver Apparel ~ 16604 ~ 2H9U7A228VA048027 ~ Service - Wheels off single or tandem axle', and 'Pamill Paving ~ 713 ~ 3HAEUMMP1NL291283 ~ Replace - Rear ramp handles'.

Week view (29 of 55 blocks) and Day view (6 of 12) are both correct. Not every block shows a VIN, because not every unit has one recorded — the fault is that any VIN appears in Month view at all.

With the switch off, no block in any view shows a VIN, so the switch itself is working and this is specific to Month view.

Expected behaviour

Month view blocks show no VIN at all, even with the switch on.

Source

Epic SV-8685 Open , story SV-8690 QA Complete (Shift Block Anatomy & Scope Labeling), and the Schedule specification (Confluence page 713031682), version 25.

Section 4.4, of the VIN line: "Line 3 (optional): VIN number, visible only when the VIN toggle is on in Filter and Display. Shown in day and week views only; month view omits it due to space constraints."

Description

On a narrow window the Schedule page slides sideways as a whole — the top navigation and the toolbar go with it — instead of only the grid scrolling, and the left-hand work order panel never folds away. A planner on a small window ends up scrolling the entire page left and right to see the end of the week while a third of the screen is still taken by the panel.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: QA branch sv8685 — https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule. Desktop browser, signed in as an Admin, with the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 selected.

  1. Open Schedule in Week view for the week of 3 August 2026, which on this shop shows 22 technician rows and 55 shift blocks.
  2. Make the browser window 960 pixels wide — the narrowest width the Schedule is meant to support.
  3. Look at the left-hand work order panel, and try scrolling the page sideways.
  4. Narrow the window further, to 900 pixels and then to 700, and look again each time.
  5. Widen it to 1680 pixels and look once more.

Current behaviour

The left-hand panel keeps the same width all the way down — at 1000, 960, 900 and 700 pixels alike. It never folds away.

The page itself is what scrolls sideways, not the grid. The page stays 1030 pixels wide however narrow the window gets, so the sideways scrollbar belongs to the whole page.

There is no sideways scroller on the grid at all.

At 1680 pixels there is no sideways scrolling, so this only appears once the window is narrowed. It happens at exactly 960 pixels, which is inside the supported range and not only an edge case. The page reports no errors at any width.

Expected behaviour

The grid — not the whole page — is what scrolls sideways, and the left-hand panel collapses once the window is narrow.

Source

Epic SV-8685 Open , story SV-8686 TESTING QA (Schedule Grid Layout & Navigation), and the Schedule specification (Confluence page 713031682), version 25.

Section 11 (Non-functional requirements), under Responsiveness: "Minimum supported width is 960px (the grid scrolls horizontally below that), and the sidebar collapses on narrow viewports." Both halves are in that one sentence.

Description

The only way to put a job on the Schedule is now to drag it. There used to be a click alternative — you clicked a small control on the work order card, the card showed as armed, and you then clicked a technician's cell to place the job. That control has gone from the current build, so anyone who cannot drag has no way to schedule at all.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: QA branch sv8685 — https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule. Desktop browser, signed in as an Admin, with the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 selected.

  1. Open Schedule in Week view for the week of 3 August 2026.
  2. Look at work order card S-12876, Pamill Paving, unit 713, 1 line, in the left-hand panel. Hover over it.
  3. Open that card's line list using the arrow on the right, and look inside it.
  4. Do the same with a multi-line card — S-13014, Fuline Enterprises, unit G30, 7 lines.
  5. Look for any button that arms a card for click placement.

Current behaviour

There is no such button anywhere — not on the card, not when hovering it, and not inside the line list. The card carries no button of any kind; its only interactive parts are the status chip and the arrow that opens the line list.

The line list holds only a back button, a search box, two scope buttons and the line rows.

It was there on an earlier build of this same branch (v3.5-be42149), where the control read 'Schedule S-12876 by click' and clicking it armed the card so a technician cell could be clicked to place the job. So this is something that has been lost, not something never built.

For a developer: the whole page was searched for any control whose name or label mentions arming or clicking to schedule, and there are none. It was checked as an Admin with the full Schedule permission, so it is not a permissions problem.

Expected behaviour

A click alternative to dragging is present, and clicking it then clicking a technician's cell places the job and opens the same scope window a drag opens.

Source

Epic SV-8685 Open , story SV-8688 TESTING QA (Drag-and-Drop Scheduling & Shift Creation), and the Schedule specification (Confluence page 713031682), version 25.

Section 11 (Non-functional requirements), under Accessibility: "drag-and-drop has a click-to-arm alternative". Section 7 says it again: "Drag-and-drop has a click-to-arm alternative for users who cannot drag."

Description

In Month view a job spread over several days is drawn as one bar, and the bar does not say whose it is. Month view has no technician rows to read the name off, unlike Day and Week, so a planner looking at the month cannot tell who a job is booked to without opening it.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: QA branch sv8685 — https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule. Desktop browser, signed in as an Admin, with the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 selected.

  1. Open Schedule and switch to Month view for August 2026.
  2. Find a job that runs over several days — it will say 'Part of a series'. On this shop, Xiriver Apparel unit 24069 (19 lines) and Kastone Solutions unit HE2-001 (7 lines) are both there.
  3. Read the bar from left to right.
  4. For a contrast, switch to Week view and look at the same job.

Current behaviour

The bar reads, for example, 'Xiriver Apparel 24069 19 Lines Part of a series', and another reads 'Kastone Solutions HE2-001 7 Lines Part of a series'. No technician name or initials appear on it at all.

Six series bars were read in Month view and none carried a technician. In Week view the technician is the row, so the name is available there — this is specific to Month view.

It is not a display setting: the VIN switch and the department filters were not the cause; the technician is simply not part of the bar's text.

Expected behaviour

The label at the start of the bar includes the technician the job is booked to.

Source

Epic SV-8685 Open , story SV-8692 QA Complete (Linked Series & Banners), and the Schedule specification (Confluence page 713031682), version 25.

Section 4.6 (Linked series and banners): "Month view: a continuous bar wrapping across week rows, labeled once at the start (with the technician), with a faded 'continues' label on later weeks, empty weekend columns (when business hours are not set for weekends)." The words in brackets are the part that is missing.

Description

When you hover a shift that has a clash, the tooltip does warn you, but the warning sits at the very bottom, several rows below the customer name, and the customer name row carries no warning mark. The customer name is the first thing anyone reads, so a planner scanning quickly can miss that the shift clashes at all.

Steps to reproduce

Environment: QA branch sv8685 — https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule. Desktop browser, signed in as an Admin, with the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 selected.

  1. Open Schedule in Week view for the week of 3 August 2026.
  2. Find a shift with an amber warning triangle on the block. The one used here was Brabay Maintenance, VIN C44ECN300699, Tuesday 4 August, 27 lines, technician Ayesha Khan — it has three clash reasons at once.
  3. Hover over the middle of that block and wait for the tooltip. Hover the block, not the warning triangle, which has a small tooltip of its own.
  4. Read the tooltip from the top down.

Current behaviour

The first row is just the customer name — 'Brabay Maintenance' — with no warning mark beside it.

The warning appears only in the last row, as 'Starts before working hours - Extends past working hours - Double-booked' with a triangle beside it. The warning text is amber, which is correct.

The rest of the tooltip renders correctly — customer, VIN, date and time, technician, line list and progress bar — so only the position of the warning mark is wrong.

Expected behaviour

The warning mark sits next to the customer name on the first line of the tooltip. The reason line in amber at the bottom is correct and stays.

Source

Epic SV-8685 Open , story SV-8695 TESTING QA (Shift Detail Modal & Hover Tooltips), and the Schedule specification (Confluence page 713031682), version 25.

Section 4.13 (Hover tooltips) sets out the order of the tooltip's contents: "Shift tooltip: customer name (plus the conflict icon if conflicted); unit, vehicle, and VIN; date and time range; technician; scope summary ('N lines - Xh'); the individual line names as a short list capped at 3 with a '+N more lines' row (no line statuses); a time-logged progress bar ('X / Yh'); and the conflict reason in amber when conflicted." So the reason at the bottom is right; what is missing is the icon beside the customer name on the first line.

Environment QA branch — sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders, Partsdesktop.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the Work Orders, Parts,Reports pages (desktop).
  2. Look at each filter chip in the filter bar (Status, Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, Asset on Site).

Actual Result
The chips show the filter name and a chevron only — there is no leading type-icon before the name.

Expected Result
Each filter chip should display a leading type-icon before the name (e.g. status glyph for Status, person for Customer, wrench for Lead Technician, headset for Service Advisor, box for Asset on Site), per the design and Branko's ruling.

Confirmed by Branko on SV-8904 Done (2026-08-06): "Filter chips should have icons for each filter." This also aligns with Stefan's "design is source of truth" call (the design shows the leading icons).

Impact
Filter chips do not match the design; the leading type-icons that aid at-a-glance recognition of each filter are missing.

Reference

  • Decision: SV-8904 Done (Branko, 2026-08-06) — chips should have a leading icon per filter
  • Design (source of truth): Figma / Claude filter bar (chips with leading icons)
  • PRD Filters v1.6 / Confluence v18 (https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/shopviewapp/pages/572030978/Filters) — S1-R3 (currently says "name + chevron" only; pending update by product to include the icon)
  • Test case: C29558 (currently asserts "no picture icon" — to be updated to require the leading icon)
  • Parent note: parented to SV-8786 Ready for QA (Filter Bar Layout & Visibility).
